messages:
olivia: quick checkin after reading the RFC follow-up thread. i want to propose a slightly different surface: keep items-first iterator but add an explicit failure_mode and a cheap checkpoint token. failure_mode choices: `stop` (raise on fatal page error), `resume` (try to continue skipping failed pages), `best_effort` (yield what we have, then surface a consolidated error at end). recommendations?

sam: i like explicit modes. default should be `stop` so we don't surprise apps that expect completeness.

ben: question: how do you define a "failed page" vs transient fetch error? are we going to rely solely on transport retry exhaustion?

olivia: transport will expose a per-fetch result object with attempts and last_error. we treat retry exhaustion as a failed page. but we can also classify by HTTP code or server hint header.

priya: idea: emit a lightweight checkpoint token periodically (e.g., every 100 items or when next_page_token changes). token = base64(route + last_page_token + seq). caller can store it and resume later. helps resume semantics when failure_mode=resumable.

sam: that helps bulk consumers. need to document that checkpoint tokens are opaque and not guaranteed stable across model/backend changes.

ben: idempotency: for APIs that mutate behind pagination (rare), we should support an `idempotency_token` header per original request or per-item derived token. propose: by default we do per-request idempotency if client passes `idempotency_key`. if none provided and endpoint marked non-idempotent, disallow transparent retries.

olivia: agreed. add `allow_transparent_retries: false` when `non_idempotent:true` or when idempotency_key missing. make the flag explicit in the call options.

priya: prefetch/backpressure: expose `max_inflight_pages` and `max_prefetch_items`. transport maintains a semaphore. default max_inflight_pages=2, max_prefetch_items=500. callers can override per-call.

sam: how to balance head-of-line blocking? if a long tail page is slow but others are fast, we should let iterator deliver items from fast pages while retrying the slow one. that argues for independent page pipelines (concurrency) with reordering allowed?

ben: reordering is tricky for order-sensitive streams. add call option `preserve_order: true|false`. if preserve_order=true, we buffer until earlier pages resolved. else yield as available. default preserve_order=true for list endpoints unless explicitly set.

olivia: for SDK ergonomics: Go -> Iterator struct with Next()/Item()/Err(), supports Context cancel. Python -> sync iterator and async iterator (list_x, async_list_x). TS -> AsyncGenerator plus optional `.cancel()` helper via returned controller `{generator, cancel}`. map cancel to AbortSignal underneath.

priya: cancellation semantics: caller cancel -> cancel in-flight fetches, stop spawning new fetches, flush buffered yielded items (still deliver already-yielded), then if failure_mode=best_effort surface consolidated `Cancelled` or `PartialResult` error depending on config.

sam: telemetry: emit events: `iter.start`, `page.fetch.attempt`, `page.fetch.succeed`, `page.fetch.fail`, `iter.checkpoint`, `iter.cancel`, `iter.end` with fields: route, attempts, duration, items_yielded, failure_mode. this is critical for Console teams.

ben: tests: add fuzz tests that vary page sizes, inject transient errors mid-prefetch, simulate reordering, and assert invariants for preserve_order true/false. also add resume tests using checkpoint token.

olivia: developer migration: feature-flag rollout. start with opt-in param `flat_iter=true` on client. run cross-lang canaries and measure error surface and user confusion. propose 2-week canary then default flip with a 1-month deprecation window for page APIs.

priya: small API sketch for call options: `client.list_things({prefetch:2, max_inflight_pages:2, max_prefetch_items:200, preserve_order:true, failure_mode:"stop", idempotency_key:"abc", allow_transparent_retries:true, dedupe_on:"id"})`. make sure type checks across py/ts/go.

sam: edge-case: dup items across page boundaries. if dedupe_on provided, we maintain a seen-set and drop duplicates. warn about memory cost. maybe provide a streaming bloom-filter option to bound memory?

ben: bloom-filter is neat but probabilistic. add `dedupe_mode: exact|probabilistic` with params. default exact.

nathan: i'll take ownership of a Go prototype for the Iterator that supports preserve_order flag and context cancellation.

olivia: thanks. action items: @nathan prototype Go, @priya add TS generator/controller wrapper + AbortSignal mapping, @sam own telemetry schema, @ben write conformance/fuzz tests, i'll update RFC with API sketch and rollout plan. linking follow-up doc in thread when done. :sparkles: 

sdk-ci-bot: branch rfc/flat-iter-impl CI green: https://ci.internal/redwood/1250

olivia: wrapping up
